jobs.title: Portfolio Management Consultant
jobs.description:
Job Description:

Providing for loved ones, planning rewarding retirements, saving enough for whatever lies ahead – our policyholders count on us to be there when it matters most. It’s a big ask, but it’s one that we have the power to deliver when we work together. We collaborate and innovate – pushing one another to transform not just Pacific Life, but the entire industry for the better. Why? Because it’s the right thing to do. Pacific Life is more than a job, it’s a career with purpose. It’s a career where you have the support, balance, and resources to make a positive impact on the future – including your own.

We’re actively seeking a talented Project Portfolio Management Consultant to join our Portfolio and Program Management team in Newport Beach, CA. This role is hybrid. We believe in empowering our employees to get work done both in and out of the office.

As a Project Portfolio Management Consultant, you’ll move Pacific Life — and your career — forward by leading portfolio management practices that ensure the right initiatives are prioritized, monitored , and executed in alignment with strategic objectives , business value, and capacity. This P5 consultant role is recognized as an expert-level individual contributor within and beyond the function. You will fill a role within the Workforce Division, partnering with project, program, portfolio, product, finance, strategy, business, and technology leaders to strengthen portfolio governance, forecasting, roadmap visibility, and decision-making discipline.

How you’ll help move us forward:
- Lead portfolio management rhythms and governance forums that help senior leaders prioritize investments, track health, and make timely trade-off decisions.

- Translate divisional and functional strategies into integrated portfolio roadmaps that connect demand, funding, capacity, dependencies, milestones, risks, and expected outcomes.

- Support the end-to-end portfolio lifecycle, including planning, initiation, prioritization, resource and capacity inputs, execution monitoring, benefits realization, and value tracking.

- Translate Workforce Division strategies into actionable portfolio initiatives that advance growth, innovation, operational excellence, and measurable business outcomes.

- Maintain awareness of business, market, and operational trends to help identify portfolio opportunities, risks, and trade-offs.

- Partner with business, finance, strategy, technology, product, program, and project leaders to ensure project and program work is prioritized, monitored , and executed in support of strategic objectives and business value.

- Develop and continuously improve portfolio management standards, practices, templates, reporting, and operating routines to advance PPM maturity across the organization.

- Analyze portfolio performance, capacity, financials, risks, issues, and dependencies to surface insights, options, and recommendations for decision-makers .

- Drive transparency across portfolio health, value realization, and delivery confidence through concise executive-ready communications, dashboards, summaries, and decision materials.

- Act as a trusted advisor and thought partner to stakeholders, applying broad business perspective and portfolio expertise to solve complex, cross-functional challenges.

- Coach and guide colleagues with less experience, helping teams adopt consistent practices while adapting approaches to business context and delivery needs.

The experience you bring:
- 10+ years of experience in portfolio management, program management, project management, strategic planning, governance, or related business transformation roles.

- 4-year degree or equivalent experience.

- Demonstrated expertise in managing or enabling complex portfolios of initiatives across business and technology teams in a matrixed environment.

- Proven ability to interpret internal or external business issues and recommend process , product, service, or operating model improvements with broad business impact.

- Strong knowledge of portfolio and project management methodologies, techniques, and best practices, with the ability to apply them pragmatically across business contexts.

- Strong executive communication, facilitation, prioritization, and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to influence decisions without direct authority.

- Experience with portfolio governance, integrated roadmapping , demand intake, prioritization, capacity planning, dependency management, financial stewardship, risk management, and value tracking.

- Strong analytical skills, including the ability to synthesize quantitative and qualitative inputs into clear insights, options, and recommendations.

- Experience using portfolio, project, and collaboration tools such as Planview, Smartsheet, Azure DevOps, Jira, Confluence, Microsoft Project, SharePoint, Teams, OneNote, PowerPoint, or similar platforms.

- Experience in regulated industries such as insurance, financial services, healthcare, or similar environments preferred.

What makes you stand out:
- Project Management Professional (PMP)®, Program Management Professional ( PgMP )®, Portfolio Management Professional ( PfMP )®, or PMI Agile Certified Practitioner (PMI- ACP)® .

- SAFe ® Agilist (SA), Lean Portfolio Management, Certified ScrumMaster (CSM), Certified Scrum Professional (CSP), or similar Agile / Lean certification.

- Experience in implementation and roll out of Portfolio Management and Project Portfolio Management tools such as Planview, Clarity or similar platforms.

- Experience implementing or maturing portfolio governance, cross-portfolio planning, value management, and executive portfolio reporting practices.

- Consulting experience or demonstrated ability to advise leaders, shape ambiguous problems, and build coalitions around pragmatic solutions.

- Demonstrated ability to build a compelling narrative, facilitate working sessions, influence senior leaders, and help drive decisions to conclusion in ambiguous environments.

- Advanced executive storytelling, data visualization, and decision support capabilities.

What Success Looks Like:
- Portfolio decisions are grounded in clear strategy, capacity, value, risk, dependency, and funding insights.

- Roadmaps and governance routines remain current, useful, and actionable — not theoretical.

- Leaders have timely visibility into portfolio health, trade-offs, and decisions needed to maintain momentum.

- Teams use consistent portfolio practices while adapting execution approaches to business context .

- Risks, issues, and dependencies are surfaced early and managed through transparent ownership and escalation paths.

- Portfolio management maturity advances through practical standards, continuous improvement, and trusted stakeholder partnerships.

​
You can be who you are.

People come first here. We’re committed to an inclusive workforce. Learn more about how we create a welcoming work environment through Inclusion at www.pacificlife.com. What’s life like at Pacific Life? Visit Instagram.com/lifeatpacificlife.

jobs.title: Director, Treasury Systems Support
jobs.description:
Job Description:

Pacific Life is seeking a Director, Treasury Systems Support to lead the strategy, implementation, and ongoing optimization of treasury technology platforms supporting our global Treasury organization. This role plays a critical part in enabling resilient operations, real‑time cash intelligence, and strong risk and control environments through modern, scalable technology.

How you’ll help move us forward:

As the Director, Treasury Systems Support, you will have end‑to‑end ownership of treasury technology platforms, including Treasury Management Systems (TMS), payment hubs, and bank connectivity solutions. You will define the treasury technology roadmap, ensure operational excellence, and partner across Treasury, Finance, IT, Risk, and the broader enterprise to deliver solutions aligned with business objectives and regulatory requirements.

You will also lead and develop a high‑performing treasury systems team, strengthening technical capability, governance, and judgment across the function.

What you’ll do
Treasury Technology Strategy & Ownership
- Own the full lifecycle of treasury systems, including TMS, payment platforms, and bank connectivity solutions.
- Define and maintain the treasury technology roadmap aligned with Treasury strategy, enterprise architecture standards, and regulatory requirements.
- Lead the evaluation, selection, and implementation of new systems, upgrades, enhancements, and integrations with ERP and finance platforms.

Systems Operations & Production Support
- Ensure high availability, performance, and reliability of treasury platforms.
- Oversee daily production support, including incident management, root‑cause analysis, and vendor coordination.
- Lead disaster recovery, backup, and business continuity planning for treasury systems.

Payments & Bank Connectivity
- Enable payment processing across ACH, wires, RTGS, checks, and emerging payment rails.
- Oversee bank connectivity methods such as SWIFT, host‑to‑host, APIs, and secure file transfers.
- Ensure effective fraud prevention controls, sanctions screening, and approval workflows are embedded within systems.

Data, Reporting & Analytics
- Ensure treasury systems deliver accurate, timely, and auditable data to support cash positioning, forecasting, liquidity stress testing, and debt and investment reporting.
- Partner with Treasury and Finance stakeholders to enhance dashboards, automation, and data quality.

Risk, Controls & Compliance
- Ensure treasury systems meet internal control and regulatory requirements, including SOX, cybersecurity, access controls, and data governance standards.
- Oversee user access provisioning and segregation of duties.
- Support internal and external audits and lead remediation of system‑related findings.

Vendor & Third‑Party Management
- Serve as the primary relationship owner for treasury technology vendors and partners (e.g., FIS, Kyriba, SWIFT).
- Support contract management, SLA monitoring, performance reviews, and roadmap alignment.
- Coordinate system testing and connectivity changes with banking partners.

Cross‑Functional Partnership
- Act as a bridge between Treasury and IT, translating business needs into scalable technical solutions.
- Collaborate closely with Accounting, FP&A, Investments, Corporate Finance, Enterprise Architecture, Information Security, and Risk.
- Support enterprise initiatives impacting Treasury, including ERP transformations and data strategy programs.

Leadership & Governance
- Lead, mentor, and develop treasury systems analysts and support staff.
- Establish operating models, governance forums, documentation standards, and best practices for change and release management.
- Promote continuous improvement and operational excellence across the treasury systems function.

The experience you bring
- 10+ years of experience in Treasury, Finance, or Technology roles, with at least 5 years in a leadership capacity.
- Demonstrated experience implementing and managing Treasury Management Systems (e.g., Kyriba, FIS, SAP Treasury).
- Strong understanding of banking connectivity (SWIFT, APIs), payment platforms, ERP integrations, and treasury operations.
- Solid knowledge of cash positioning, liquidity management, short‑term borrowing and investing, and counterparty risk.
- Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, or a related field.
- Certified Treasury Professional (CTP) designation is preferred.

What makes you stand out
- Strong analytical and problem‑solving skills with the ability to translate complex requirements into practical solutions.
- Effective communicator who can engage with senior leaders and external partners.
- Proven ability to lead teams, manage change, and operate effectively in a complex, regulated environment.
- Operational excellence mindset with strong program and project management capabilities.

jobs.title: Institutional Marketing Strategy Director
jobs.description:
Job Description:

Pacific Life is investing in bright, agile, and diverse new talent to contribute to our mission of innovating our business and creating a superior customer experience. We're actively seeking a talented Institutional Marketing Strategy Director
to join our Institutional Retirement Solutions Group (IRSG).

This role can be based in Newport Beach, CA, Omaha, NE, or another approved Pacific Life office location.

As Institutional Marketing Strategy Director, you will serve as a strategic marketing partner to IRSG leadership, helping translate business strategy, market dynamics, customer needs, and competitive intelligence into clear marketing priorities and differentiated market strategies.

The role spans Pacific Life's institutional retirement businesses, including Pension Risk Transfer (PRT), Defined Contribution Lifetime Income (DCLI), Stable Value, and emerging retirement solutions. You will help leadership determine where Pacific Life should focus, how the organization should position itself, which audiences and opportunities matter most, and how marketing can influence growth.

You will bring together market intelligence, customer and audience insights, competitive understanding, positioning, messaging, thought leadership, and go-to-market strategy to help IRSG build preference and strengthen its position in the marketplace.

This is a highly visible leadership role at the intersection of business strategy, market intelligence, marketing strategy, and growth . The ideal candidate is equally comfortable analyzing a market, challenging a business assumption, shaping a narrative, and translating strategy into action.

How You'll Help Move Us Forward:

Lead and Evolve Institutional Marketing Strategy
- Own, activate and evolve the established IRSG marketing strategy, ensuring it remains aligned with business priorities, market opportunities, customer needs, and the maturity of each business.
- Partner with senior business and functional leaders to identify the markets, audiences, opportunities, and priorities where marketing can have the greatest impact.
- Translate business strategies and established marketing priorities into actionable audience strategies, positioning, messaging, content, and go-to-market recommendations.
- Evolve strategic direction along with business goals and strategies for the Institutional content roadmap, ensuring priority themes, audiences, and timing are informed by business objectives, market and customer insights, and go-to-market needs, while partnering with the broader marketing team on development and execution.
- Develop business-specific marketing approaches that recognize the distinct needs and market positions of Pension Risk Transfer (PRT), Defined Contribution Lifetime Income (DCLI), Stable Value, and emerging institutional businesses while maintaining alignment with the established IRSG narrative and strategy.
- Monitor market, business, and competitive developments and recommend strategic adjustments as priorities and opportunities evolve.
- Lead ongoing marketing planning and prioritization, establishing clear trade-offs and aligning marketing resources, investments, and activity to the highest-value business priorities and measurable growth objectives.

Drive Market Intelligence and Competitive Insights
- Serve as a strategic consumer of market, customer, and competitive intelligence, bringing relevant insights into IRSG marketing and business discussions.
- Partner with internal strategy, analytics, research, product, distribution, and other teams to identify and leverage available market and customer insights.
- Monitor key industry, competitor, regulatory, and market developments and assess their implications for IRSG marketing priorities and business objectives.
- Identify gaps in market or customer understanding and help define the research or analysis needed to inform strategic decisions.
- Translate complex market and competitive information into clear, actionable insights and recommendations for business and marketing leaders.
- Bring an external perspective to marketing strategy, helping identify emerging opportunities, shifts in audience needs, and potential areas of differentiation.

Steward Positioning, Messaging, and Market Narrative
- Serve as a steward of IRSG's established positioning, value proposition, and overarching narrative, ensuring they are consistently and effectively applied across marketing initiatives.
- Translate established positioning and value propositions into audience-specific messaging and marketing strategies for PRT, DCLI, Stable Value, and emerging institutional businesses.
- Partner with business and product leaders to apply the established positioning to priority initiatives, launches, campaigns, and market opportunities.
- Identify opportunities where changing market dynamics, customer needs, or competitive activity may warrant refinement or evolution of existing positioning and messaging.
- Ensure consistency and differentiation across institutional marketing efforts while allowing messaging to reflect the distinct needs and maturity of each business.
- Partner with other marketing teams to bring the established positioning and narrative to life across channels and experiences.

Guide Institutional Thought Leadership
- Provide strategic direction for institutional thought leadership priorities, ensuring they align with the established IRSG marketing strategy, narrative, positioning, and business objectives.
- Partner with business leaders and subject matter experts to identify priority topics and opportunities where thought leadership can support market engagement and business goals.
- Translate business priorities and market developments into recommendations for thought leadership themes, audiences, channels, and timing.
- Partner with operations, digital and other marketing resources to ensure thought leadership initiatives are strategically focused and effectively executed.
- Advise on executive visibility, industry engagement, conferences, speaking opportunities, and other external opportunities based on business and marketing priorities.
- Evaluate the effectiveness and relevance of thought leadership efforts and recommend adjustments as business priorities and market dynamics evolve.

Inform Go-to-Market and Growth Initiatives
- Provide strategic marketing leadership for new products, market expansion efforts, strategic initiatives, and emerging growth opportunities.
- Assess market readiness, audience needs, competitive dynamics, and differentiation opportunities to inform go-to-market strategies.
- Partner with product, distribution, communications, analytics, digital, and other marketing teams to translate strategy into execution.
- Help define target audiences, market priorities, value propositions, and channel strategies for priority initiatives.
- Provide strategic marketing counsel on business cases, executive presentations, strategic communications, and other high-priority business materials.
- Identify opportunities to strengthen the connection between marketing activity and the customer and distribution journeys that influence growth.

Measure Impact and Evolve the Strategy
- Establish frameworks for evaluating marketing effectiveness, market impact, and progress against strategic priorities.
- Define meaningful KPIs for marketing strategies, thought leadership initiatives, market engagement, and priority growth programs.
- Use data, analytics, research, and business results to evaluate what is working and where strategy should evolve.
- Regularly assess the effectiveness of marketing investments and recommend changes in priorities, resources, or approach.
- Champion a culture of accountability, learning, and continuous improvement across institutional marketing.

The Experience You Bring
- 10+ years of experience in strategic marketing, financial services marketing, institutional marketing, business strategy, consulting, product marketing, market intelligence, or a related discipline.
- Demonstrated experience developing marketing strategies that are directly connected to business growth and strategic priorities.
- Strong understanding of institutional financial services, retirement markets, insurance, investments, asset management, or related B2B financial markets.
- Experience translating market, customer, competitive, and business intelligence into strategic recommendations.
- Proven ability to influence senior leaders and build alignment across complex, matrixed organizations.
- Experience developing positioning, segmentation, value propositions, messaging, go-to-market strategies, or related strategic marketing frameworks.
- Exceptional communication, presentation, and storytelling skills, with the ability to make complex subjects clear and compelling.
- Strong analytical and critical-thinking skills, with the ability to move from insight to recommendation to action.
- Demonstrated ability to operate strategically while working effectively with teams responsible for execution.

The experience you bring:
- Experience in Pension Risk Transfer, Defined Contribution, retirement income, Stable Value, asset management, insurance, or adjacent institutional markets.
- Experience working with institutional buyers and influencers, including consultants, intermediaries, advisors, plan sponsors, institutional investors, recordkeepers, or retirement-focused organizations.
- Experience building or leading market intelligence, competitive intelligence, customer insight, or strategic planning capabilities.
- Experience developing thought leadership strategies and executive positioning programs.
- Experience supporting large-scale growth, transformation, innovation, or new-market initiatives.
- MBA or advanced degree preferred.

What Makes You Stand Out
- You think beyond the marketing function. You understand how markets, customers, competitors, products, distribution, and business strategy come together to create growth.
- You are naturally curious. You want to understand what is changing in the market, why it matters, and what Pacific Life should do about it.
- You turn complexity into clarity. You can take a complicated business issue or market dynamic and turn it into a clear point of view, strategic recommendation, or compelling story.
- You connect strategy to action. You know when to stay at the strategic level and when to translate strategy into specific priorities for the teams responsible for execution.
- You can influence without owning everything. You build trust with senior leaders and cross-functional partners and can move work forward in a highly matrixed environment.
- You understand that differentiation is earned. You look beyond claims and messaging to identify the capabilities, perspectives, and market opportunities that can create meaningful competitive advantage.
- You bring executive presence. You are comfortable challenging assumptions, presenting recommendations, and engaging with senior leaders on complex business and market issues.

Why This Role Matters

This role serves as the strategic marketing connector across IRSG—bringing together business priorities, market intelligence, customer insight, competitive understanding, and marketing execution to ensure the organization's marketing strategy remains aligned to business needs and responsive to the marketplace.
With the IRSG marketing strategy and overarching narrative established, the Director will help activate and evolve that strategy across Pension Risk Transfer, Defined Contribution Lifetime Income, Stable Value, and emerging retirement solutions. The role will translate strategic priorities into focused marketing initiatives, inform future planning through ongoing market and competitive intelligence, and ensure that marketing efforts are differentiated, audience-relevant, and connected to measurable business outcomes.

The position will also look beyond the current roadmap, identifying emerging market opportunities, shifts in customer and competitive dynamics, and future strategic needs that should inform the next evolution of IRSG's marketing strategy.

Ultimately, this role ensures that marketing operates as a strategic business partner—not simply an execution function —helping IRSG strengthen market position, build preference, and support sustainable growth.

jobs.description:
Job Description:

Providing for loved ones, planning rewarding retirements, saving enough for whatever lies ahead – our policyholders count on us to be there when it matters most. It’s a big ask, but it’s one that we have the power to deliver when we work together. We collaborate and innovate – pushing one another to transform not just Pacific Life, but the entire industry for the better. Why? Because it’s the right thing to do. Pacific Life is more than a job, it’s a career with purpose. It’s a career where you have the support, balance, and resources to make a positive impact on the future – including your own.

We’re actively seeking a talented Portfolio Strategy & Transformation Leader to join our Strategic Management & Services team in Newport Beach, California. This role follows a hybrid schedule of four days in the office. If you are not currently located near our office, we offer comprehensive relocation assistance. As a Portfolio Strategy & Transformation Leader, you will lead the Consumer Markets Division’s (CMD) Portfolio and Program Management Office (PPMO) and play a critical role in translating strategy into disciplined execution and measurable business outcomes. You will oversee a complex portfolio spanning strategic transformation, business-critical initiatives, AI-enabled programs, and ongoing investments that support the strength and evolution of Pacific Life’s life insurance and annuity businesses.

This is an opportunity to lead at the center of one of Pacific Life’s most established and consequential businesses. The PPMO is where the division’s strategic priorities become actionable programs, where investments are prioritized and resourced, and where diverse teams come together to deliver meaningful outcomes for customers and distribution partners. As a member of the Strategic Management & Services leadership team, you will serve as a trusted advisor to senior business and technology leaders, bring transparency to complex decisions, and help shape how Pacific Life operates in an increasingly connected enterprise environment. You will lead an established organization of approximately 35 portfolio, program, project, and agile professionals, including five to six direct reports, while building the capabilities required to support the division’s future growth and transformation.

How you’ll help move us forward:
- Lead the Consumer Markets Division’s portfolio management and PPMO function, ensuring strategic investments, transformation initiatives, and business-critical programs align with divisional priorities and measurable business outcomes
- Establish and continuously strengthen portfolio planning, prioritization, capacity management, resource allocation, investment governance, and benefits realization practices
- Oversee delivery of the division’s most complex, high-impact programs, including multiyear transformation initiatives supporting underwriting and new business, operations, sales, and distribution capabilities
- Provide senior leaders with clear portfolio insights, risk transparency, decision support, and executive-level reporting that improve alignment, accountability, and predictability
- Partner across the Consumer Markets Division, Pacific Life Technology, People Experience, Finance, Risk, and other enterprise functions to resolve barriers, align priorities, and accelerate business outcomes

- Represent the Consumer Markets Division in enterprise portfolio planning, governance, and prioritization activities, helping build stronger connections and more integrated ways of working across Pacific Life

The experience you bring:

- Demonstrated ability to balance strategic direction with effective delegation, empowering leaders to execute while maintaining accountability for enterprise outcomes

- Demonstrated success leading complex, cross-functional portfolios and transformation initiatives with significant organizational, financial, or customer impact
- Deep expertise in portfolio planning, prioritization, investment governance, capacity and resource management, risk management, and benefits realization
- Experience overseeing a portfolio that includes both strategic transformation initiatives and essential business operations
- Proven ability to translate business strategy into executable priorities, delivery roadmaps, governance structures, and measurable outcomes
- Strong financial and business acumen, including experience evaluating investments, managing portfolio tradeoffs, and maintaining accountability for the effective use of resources
- Executive-level communication and influence skills, with the ability to bring clarity to complex issues, challenge constructively, and advise senior leaders across business and technology organizations
- Demonstrated experience building, leading, and developing high-performing teams through transformation, growth, and organizational change
- Ability to operate effectively in an evolving environment where success requires sound judgment, curiosity, adaptability, and a willingness to build new solutions rather than rely solely on established playbooks

What makes you stand out:
- Leadership experience within financial services, insurance, wealth management, or another highly regulated industry
- Experience leading transformation across life insurance, annuity, customer operations, underwriting, sales, or distribution functions.
- Experience leveraging AI, automation, data, and modern delivery practices to improve decision-making, execution, and business outcomes

jobs.title: VP, Head of Enterprise Program Management Office
jobs.description:
Job Description:

We are actively seeking a talented VP, Head of Enterprise Program Management Office (ePMO) to join Pacific Life in Newport Beach, CA reporting to the EVP, Chief Financial Officer.  In this role, you will build and lead a new enterprise center of excellence that strengthens how Pacific Life prioritizes, governs, and delivers its most important strategic initiatives.

This leader will establish enterprise-wide portfolio and program management standards through a hub-and-spoke model, serving as the enterprise Hub while enabling divisions and functions to retain the agility and subject-matter expertise needed to execute within their businesses. The division and function PMOs will maintain direct alignment to their respective leaders and operate as the spokes of the model, with a dotted-line relationship to the ePMO.

Success will require an enterprise mindset, strong executive influence, practical transformation leadership, and the ability to create commitment across a highly matrixed international organization. This leader will build the ePMO team, operating model, governance forums, capabilities, and performance discipline needed to translate strategy into measurable outcomes.

How you’ll help move us forward:

Build the Enterprise PMO and Center of Excellence
- Create the ePMO vision, mandate, operating model, roadmap, and service portfolio in alignment with enterprise strategy and business priorities.
- Build and lead a high-performing team with the portfolio, program, change, analytics, and governance capabilities required to support enterprise priorities.
- Establish the ePMO as a practical center of excellence that provides standards, tools, expertise, coaching, and decision support without adding unnecessary bureaucracy.
- Define clear roles, decision rights, engagement models, and escalation paths across the hub-and-spoke model, with direct accountability for executing the enterprise Hub and enabling effective coordination with division/function PMOs.

Enterprise Portfolio Governance and Prioritization
- Establish an enterprise-wide portfolio governance framework that connects strategic priorities, investments, capacity, risks, dependencies, and expected business value.
- Partner with executive leaders to evaluate, sequence, and prioritize initiatives using transparent criteria and enterprise-level tradeoffs.
- Design and facilitate executive governance forums that enable timely decisions, resolve cross-enterprise constraints, and maintain accountability for outcomes.
- Create a consistent approach for initiative intake, business cases, stage gates, health assessments, benefits realization, and closure.

Standards, Methods, and Delivery Excellence
- Develop scalable standards, playbooks, templates, and minimum controls for portfolio, program, and project management across the organization.
- Establish common definitions and reporting practices for scope, milestones, financials, resources, risks, issues, dependencies, and value realization.
- Implement an appropriate mix of agile, hybrid, and traditional delivery disciplines based on initiative complexity, risk, and business need.
- Lead independent health reviews and recovery planning for strategically important initiatives when greater enterprise support or intervention is needed.

Matrixed Global Leadership and Partnership
- Create a strong ePMO community across the enterprise by leading the Hub and connecting division/functional PMOs as spokes through a consistent dotted-line model.
- Influence senior leaders without direct authority and build shared ownership for enterprise standards, portfolio transparency, and delivery outcomes.
- Balance enterprise consistency with regional, regulatory, business, and functional requirements across a complex global financial services environment.
- Partner closely with Strategy, Finance, Risk, Technology, Data, Operations, People Experience, and business leaders to connect strategic intent to execution.
- Partner with People Experience to encourage ways of working and leadership practices that enable Execution Excellence across the enterprise.

Insights, Technology, and Continuous Improvement
- Develop executive dashboards and concise portfolio narratives that surface progress, decisions, interdependencies, risk, capacity, and value.
- Use portfolio data and scenario analysis to improve investment decisions, resource allocation, and sequencing of enterprise work.
- Advance the use of modern project portfolio management platforms, workflow automation, data, and AI-enabled tools to improve visibility and execution.
- Build enterprise program management capability through assessment, learning, communities of practice, coaching, and talent development.

The experience you bring:
- 15+ years of progressive leadership experience in enterprise portfolio management, transformation, strategy execution, program management, or a related discipline, including significant experience leading complex enterprise initiatives.
- Demonstrated success building, transforming, or resetting an enterprise PMO, portfolio management, or transformation function, including establishing the mandate, operating model, governance routines, standards, and adoption roadmap.
- Experience leading in financial services, insurance, or another highly regulated industry; strong understanding of governance, risk, controls, and regulatory considerations.
- Proven ability to operate across a highly matrixed, international organization and influence executive stakeholders, business leaders, and functional partners without relying on direct authority.
- Experience building and developing high-performing teams and leading a hub-and-spoke PMO model, including direct accountability for the enterprise Hub and dotted-line relationships with division/function PMOs.
- Track record building high-performing teams and communities of practice, while coaching, teaching, and enabling leaders and project teams to adopt practical portfolio, program, and project management best practices.
- Expertise establishing governance frameworks with broad organizational adoption, including enterprise portfolio governance, investment prioritization, resource and capacity planning, financial management, risk and dependency management, executive reporting, and benefits realization.
- Strong business and financial acumen, with the ability to connect strategy, execution, financial outcomes, organizational capacity planning, investment choices, execution risk, and measurable enterprise value.
- Exceptional executive presence, relationship-building, communication, and influence skills, including the ability to simplify complex information, facilitate difficult tradeoff decisions, and shape executive investment and prioritization decisions.
- Bachelor’s degree required; an advanced degree such as an MBA and relevant credentials such as PMP, PgMP, PfMP, or equivalent are preferred.

What makes you stand out:
- You are an enterprise leader who combines strategic perspective with execution excellence—creating the discipline, accountability, and operating rhythms required to turn strategy into measurable results.
- You build trust quickly, listen well, and create alignment across leaders with different priorities, operating models, and regional needs.
- You know how to introduce standards and governance in a way that improves speed, clarity, and accountability rather than creating process for its own sake.
- You bring a relentless focus on execution quality, ensuring enterprise initiatives have clear ownership, practical milestones, visible risks, and the follow-through needed to deliver outcomes at pace.
- You are comfortable building a function from the ground up, shaping the mandate while also establishing the foundational team, routines, and tools.
- You lead with courage, integrity, partnership, and enduring strength, and create an inclusive environment where diverse perspectives improve decisions.
- You are curious about emerging technology and use data, automation, and AI responsibly to improve portfolio insight and delivery effectiveness.

jobs.title: Global Rotational Program Manager, Early Careers
jobs.description:
Job Description:

Providing for loved ones, planning rewarding retirements, saving enough for whatever lies ahead – our policyholders count on us to be there when it matters most. It’s a big ask, but it’s one that we have the power to deliver when we work together. We collaborate and innovate – pushing one another to transform not just Pacific Life, but the entire industry for the better. Why? Because it’s the right thing to do. Pacific Life is more than a job, it’s a career with purpose. It’s a career where you have the support, balance, and resources to make a positive impact on the future – including your own.

We’re actively seeking a talented Global Rotational Program Manager to join our Early Career Talent team in Charlotte, NC.

About the Early Career Team :
The Early Career Talent Team is committed to building Pacific Life's future workforce by identifying, attracting, and developing high-potential early career talent. Through internships, rotational programs, university partnerships, and strategic talent initiatives, we create opportunities for students and recent graduates to gain meaningful experience, expand their professional networks, and make a lasting impact. Our team connects emerging talent with rewarding careers while helping Pacific Life cultivate the next generation of leaders, innovators, and industry experts.

As the Global Rotational Program Manager, you will lead the strategy, design, execution, and continuous improvement of early career Pacific Life’s rotational programs globally. This role is responsible for the participant experience from onboarding through final placement, ensuring programs deliver meaningful development opportunities while supporting enterprise talent.

This position partners closely with business leaders, Talent Management,  People Business Partners, and executive sponsors to create best-in-class rotational experiences. This role owns program operations, participant development, manager partnerships, talent reviews, program placements and program outcomes.

Reporting to the Global Head of Early Career Talent Programs, the Global Rotational Program Manager will serve as the primary steward of Pacific Life’s rotational programs.

How you’ll help move us forward:
- Program Strategy & Governance: Lead the design, governance, and continuous improvement of rotational programs. Establish program standards, annual objectives, success metrics, and scalable processes that align with business and talent priorities.
- Participant Experience & Development: Manage the end-to-end participant experience including onboarding, orientation, learning curriculum, mentorship initiatives, executive exposure opportunities, cohort engagement, and career development programming.
- Professional Development, Certification & Exam Readiness: Partner with business leaders to develop and manage professional development pathways for rotational program participants. Drive certification, licensing, and exam preparation efforts including  exam support programs by coordinating study resources, tracking progress toward credential milestones, facilitating learning opportunities, and helping participants successfully advance through required development benchmarks.
- Rotation Planning & Stakeholder Management : Partner with business leaders and rotation managers to identify rotational assignments, coordinate participant transitions, establish development objectives, and ensure participants gain meaningful experiences across the organization.
- Talent Assessment and Placement:  facilitate placement discussions and recommendations while partnering with business leaders on final placement decisions, monitor participant development progress, and partner with leaders on readiness assessments and final placement decisions.
- Program Operations, Analytics & Reporting: Develop dashboards and track key metrics including retention, promotion, mobility, engagement, completion rates, and placement outcomes. Manage program communications, budgets, timelines, and continuous improvement efforts.
- Early Career Community Support: Serve as a key Early Career team presence in the Charlotte office, supporting early career programming, networking opportunities and local talent initiatives in alignment with Pacific Life's broader early career strategy.

The experience you bring:
- 5+ years of experience in early career program management, talent management, learning and development, human resources, or a related field.
- Bachelor’s degree in Human Resources, Business, Organizational Development, or a related discipline.
- Demonstrated success in designing, managing, or supporting rotational, analyst, internship, or early career programs.
- Strong stakeholder management skills with the ability to influence senior leaders and manage relationships across a matrixed organization.
- Experience facilitating talent reviews, calibration discussions, and performance evaluations
- Strong project management, organization, communication, and presentation skills.
- Proficiency in data, reporting, analytics, and emerging technologies, including AI-enabled tools, to measure program effectiveness, improve operational efficiency, enhance participant experiences, and support data-driven decision-making.
- Experience working within a multi-location and global organization, with the ability to leverage technology and digital collaboration tools to support distributed program participants and stakeholders.

jobs.title: AVP, Operations Technology Transformation Lead
jobs.description:
Job Description:

Pacific Life is seeking an experienced and visionary Assistant Vice President, Ops. Technology Transformation Lead to drive CMD’s Operations Transformation. This is a multi-year transformation and modernization initiative focused on digitization, automation, and AI enablement across CMD Operations.

This role will lead the technical strategy, architecture, and execution of Operations Transformation workstreams, partnering closely with business leaders in a “two-in-a-box” model to deliver measurable business outcomes.

This role will be located onsite in one of our office locations, preferably in Newport Beach, CA.

Key Responsibilities
Strategic Leadership
- Define and evolve the technical vision for Operations Transformation aligned with enterprise architecture and business priorities.

- Co-lead cross-functional workstreams with business counterparts, ensuring shared OKRs and outcome ownership.

- Champion modernization by decoupling legacy systems and adopting next-gen platforms and AI capabilities.

Delivery & Execution
- Lead dedicated engineering teams across Operations Transformation workstreams including FAST, IVR, GenAI, and automation.

- Oversee execution roadmaps, PI planning, and delivery metrics using agile and DevOps practices.

- Ensure tight integration with BAU technology teams while maintaining focus on transformation goals.

Architecture & Design
- Own architectural decisions across Operations Transformation platforms, ensuring scalability, modularity, and reuse.

- Guide the development of orchestration layers, self-service portals, and unified processing workflows.

Talent & Team Development
- Build and mentor high-performing technology teams, including internal staff and contractors.

- Support upskilling initiatives such as GenAI Academy and agile/DevOps training.

- Collaborate with HR and L&D on strategic workforce planning and role definition.

Qualifications
- 10+ years of experience in technology leadership roles, preferably in life and annuity insurance.

- Proven success in leading large-scale transformation programs with measurable outcomes.

- Deep expertise in enterprise architecture, cloud platforms, AI/ML, and automation.

- Strong understanding of agile delivery models, DevSecOps, and product-centric operating models.

- Exceptional communication and stakeholder management skills.

- Experience in managing hybrid teams and vendor partnerships.

Preferred Attributes
- Strategic thinker with a bias for action and continuous improvement.

- Comfortable navigating ambiguity and driving clarity in complex environments.

- Passionate about talent development and building inclusive, high-performing teams.

Be at the forefront of technology transformation, shaping the future of our enterprise and driving meaningful change. If you are a visionary leader with a passion for innovation and operational excellence, we invite you to apply.

Providing for loved ones, planning rewarding retirements, saving enough for whatever lies ahead – our policyholders count on us to be there when it matters most.
